title: Schematic density of invertible torsion points in a semiabelian variety
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $n\geq1$ write $[n]_G$ for the morphism given by adding a point to itself $n$ times using the group law. A rational point $x:\operatorname{Spec}F\to G$ [def-pc-rational-point] is killed by $n$ when $[n]_G\circ x$ is the identity point. If $Z\hookrightarrow G$ is a closed subscheme and every $x\in G(F)$ killed by some positive integer whose image in $F$ is nonzero factors through $Z$, then $Z=G$ as a closed subscheme. Rank zero tori and zero-dimensional abelian quotients are allowed.

source.place: I section 10, torsion and isogenies; supporting abelian density is the existing lem-sfb-abelian-prime-to-torsion-dense. Agent-formulated semiabelian extension and schematic version, using the torus extension definition; not asserted verbatim in Milne. Split-torus density is carried by the existing lem-sfb-smooth-diagonal-prime-to-characteristic-torsion-density.

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres] to the identity geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$. It gives an abelian variety $B$, a split torus $T=(\mathbf G_m)^r$, and homomorphisms $i:T\to G$, $q:G\to B$, with $T=\ker q$ and $q$ fppf-locally surjective. Write group laws additively, including that of $T$. The torus over any $F$-scheme $S$ is affine and finitely presented: over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ its algebra is $R[t_1,v_1,\ldots,t_r,v_r]/(t_jv_j-1)_j$. It is smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: across an affine square-zero thickening, lift the $r$ units specifying a point; if $ab=1+c$ with $c^2=0$, then $b(1-c)$ is an inverse of the lift $a$. Thus every such lift is still a point of the torus. The same calculation works for $r=0$, when the torus over $S$ is $S$. Over $F$ its Laurent monomial basis identifies its Hopf algebra with $F[\mathbf Z^r]$, with comultiplication $t^v\mapsto t^v\otimes t^v$.

source.place: Tags 0498 (definition-pseudo-torsor), 0499 (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors); extension data from the cited semiabelian definition; elementary Laurent presentation and unit-lifting calculation

proof.text: The exact sequence in step 1 is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves. Its fibre over the tautological $B$-point is the sheaf represented by $G\to B$, with the left $T_B$-action $t\cdot y=i(t)+y$. Local surjectivity supplies an fppf cover $B_a\to B$ and sections $s_a$ of $q$ on it. For every test scheme $U\to B_a$, the maps $t\mapsto s_a+i(t)$ and $y\mapsto i^{-1}(y-s_a)$ are inverse: $q(y-s_a)=0$, so the second expression is defined by the scheme-theoretic kernel. The formulas are natural in $U$ and equivariant. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-group-torsor-representability] to this sheaf and the affine smooth finitely presented group $T_B$ of step 1. It gives a representing scheme $P\to B$ which is smooth, surjective and universally open. Both $P$ and $G$ represent this same sheaf. The bijection of [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] sends the two inverse natural isomorphisms to inverse morphisms over $B$. Hence $q:G\to B$ itself has these properties. In particular $q$ is an open map.

source.place: Tags 0499 (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors), 049B (lemma-torsor), 049C (remark-fun-with-torsors); smoothness descent: descent.tex Tag 02VL; openness: morphisms.tex Tag 056G

proof.text: Let $b\in B(F)$ satisfy $nb=0$ for $n\geq1$ nonzero in $F$. The sheaf fibre $G_b$ of the epimorphism in step 1 is an fppf-locally trivial $T$-torsor: pull back its local lifts and use exactly the two translation formulas of step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-group-torsor-representability] now over $\operatorname{Spec}F$, and identify the representing scheme with $G_b$ by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. Thus $G_b$ is smooth and nonempty. Since $F$ is algebraically closed, it is separably closed: an irreducible polynomial has a root in $F$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], hence is linear, so every finite separable extension is trivial. Therefore [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] gives $y\in G_b(F)$. We have $ny\in i(T(F))$ because $q(ny)=nb=0$; write $ny=i(a)$. In each multiplicative coordinate choose an $n$th root of $a_j\in F^\times$ by algebraic closedness. These roots are nonzero, so they define $t\in T(F)$ with $nt=a$. Then $g=y-i(t)$ satisfies $q(g)=b$ and $ng=0$. For $r=0$ this correction is the identity, and the same computation applies.

source.place: Tags 0499 (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors), 049B (lemma-torsor); rational points from the cited existing density lemma; explicit root correction supplied by the agent

proof.text: For $b$ and $g$ as in step 3, translation gives an isomorphism $\tau_g:T\xrightarrow{\sim}G_b$, $t\mapsto g+i(t)$: its inverse is $y\mapsto i^{-1}(y-g)$, defined on every test scheme by $q(y-g)=0$. The inverse maps are scheme morphisms by the universal property of the kernel fibre product; their composites are identities by the group laws. Pull back $Z\hookrightarrow G$ along $T\xrightarrow{\tau_g}G_b\to G$. The result $W\hookrightarrow T$ is closed by [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image]. If $t\in T(F)$ satisfies $mt=0$ with $m\geq1$ nonzero in $F$, then $nm(g+i(t))=0$. The product $nm$ is nonzero in the field, so the hypothesis on $Z$ implies that this point factors through $Z$, equivalently $t$ factors through $W$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-diagonal-prime-to-characteristic-torsion-density], applied to the smooth diagonalizable group $T$ of step 1, every $T[m]$ for such $m$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}F$. On each copy its inclusion factors through $W$ by the preceding pointwise assertion; the component maps therefore assemble to a factorization of $T[m]\hookrightarrow T$ through $W$. The schematic-density clause of the same node now gives $W=T$. Consequently the whole scheme fibre $G_b\to G$ factors through $Z$.

source.place: Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, printed pp.231–232; Theorem 12.32, printed p.242; closed pullback: Stacks schemes.tex Tag 01JU (lemma-fibre-product-immersion)

proof.text: Suppose $U=G\setminus |Z|$ were nonempty. By step 2, $q(U)$ is a nonempty open subset of $B$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-prime-to-torsion-dense], it contains the image of a rational point $b\in B(F)$ killed by a positive integer nonzero in $F$. Thus $U$ meets the image of $G_b\to G$: for a rational point of $B$, its residue field is $F$, so $\operatorname{Spec}F\to B$ is the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)\to B$ and $G_b=G\times_B\operatorname{Spec}F$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre of $q$ over $b$; by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] its first projection is a homeomorphism onto the topological fibre $q^{-1}(b)$, which contains a point of $U$. But step 4 puts this entire fibre in $|Z|$, a contradiction. Hence $|Z|=|G|$. This also treats $B$ of dimension zero: the same density statement includes that case.

source.place: I section 10, printed pp.42–45, supporting abelian torsion input; the actual topological density statement used is the existing cited node; open-image assembly supplied by the agent

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] to the given smooth structure map $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. Its fibre is $G$, so $G$ is reduced. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq G$ has reduced ring $R$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the restriction of $Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq R$. Step 5 says $V(I)=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Apply [lem-sc-reduced-ideals-zero-intersection] with both of its ideals equal to $I$: its hypothesis $V(I)\cup V(I)=\operatorname{Spec}R$ holds, and its conclusion gives $I=I\cap I=0$. Thus $Z$ restricts to the whole of each affine open of $G$, and $Z=G$ as a closed subscheme. This is the required schematic conclusion, including the trivial group, $n=1$, and all allowed torus ranks.
